subject: Autonomy - streaming + concurrency discovery and next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Greene <alex@autonomy.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Autonomy - streaming + concurrency discovery and next steps

Alex — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the tech deep-dive.

Top pain points you shared:
- Client-facing streaming feels jittery; engineers see spikes in first-byte latency during concurrent sessions.
- p95 token latency currently ranges widely (paper trail from logs shows spikes to 700–1,200ms at peak).
- Concurrency limit on your current endpoint (self-hosted Triton cluster) is capping at ~120 steady sessions — causes queuing under burst.

Current stack you mentioned:
- Frontend: web sockets to a Node gateway (per-session affinity)
- Model host: self-hosted Triton + NVIDIA A100s, single-replica pools for cost reasons
- Cache: in-process KV cache that is cold on new sessions

Success criteria you outlined (what would make this a win):
- p95 token latency for streaming < 200ms at target concurrency (1k concurrent sessions)
- Smooth streaming UX (no >300ms inter-token jitter for 99% of sessions)
- Predictable per-hour cost (within 10% of current baseline after efficiency gains)

Proposed next steps (we can own items in bold):
1) Schedule a 60m tech deep-dive this week with your infra/ML eng team — target Tue or Wed (please confirm). **(Action: Mina to send calendar invite & agenda)**
2) Provide a short test harness and sample payloads (we’ll include a script to replay session patterns). **(Action: Karthik to share harness & runbook)**
3) Trial: we propose running a 2–3 day pilot on Redwood Dedicated to reproduce load and collect p95 & streaming-jitter metrics. We’ll include automatic KV warmup and prefix cache suggestions. **(Action: Jordan to scope pilot capacity and estimated cost)**
4) Procurement: if pilot looks good, align on reserved capacity sizing and timing. **(Action: Mina to introduce procurement thread with required docs)**

Attachments: redwood-overview.pdf (high-level), latency-metrics.csv (example metrics format)

If that matches your recollection, I’ll send the invite and the test harness this afternoon. Thanks — excited to help stabilize streaming UX here.

—
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
[Attachment: redwood-overview.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Alex Greene <alex@autonomy.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Autonomy - streaming + concurrency discovery and next steps

Thanks Mina — that recap is accurate and helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The 700–1,200ms numbers are per-token for the "first-byte" step when KV cache is cold; once warmed, token times drop to ~120–180ms but we see the cold-starts often on user session churn.
- Our Triton pool is multi-tenant with horizontal autoscaling disabled today (manual scale only).
- Target concurrency for phase 1 is 800 sessions (we used 1k as an aspirational number in the call but 800 is what procurement will budget for initially).

We can do Tue 2027-08-16 10:00 PT for the deep-dive. I’ll loop in our infra lead (procurement asked to be cc’d once we have pilot cost).

Also: can you include a sample comparison table (expected p95 improvements) for the pilot so procurement has something to review?

—
Alex Greene
Head of Product Engineering | Autonomy Inc
alex@autonomy.ai

Subject: Re: Autonomy - streaming + concurrency discovery and next steps

Alex — perfect, I’ll lock Tue 2027-08-16 10:00 PT. Calendar invite + agenda sent.

Per your ask — attached is a short one-pager with expected delta for the pilot (ballpark):
- Baseline (your current Triton pool): p95 token latency: 700–1,200ms (cold), 120–180ms (warm)
- Redwood Dedicated pilot (default config + KV warmup): predicted p95 token latency: 180–220ms at 800 concurrent sessions
- Streaming jitter (inter-token) expected to be <200ms 99% of the time with our continuous batching + async dispatching

Notes/assumptions:
- We’ll run a 48h workload replay using your session traces; results depend on model size and sequence length distribution.
- Pilot cost estimate attached (Jordan’s doc) — assumes 2x A100-equivalent capacity for the 48h run.

Next items before the deep-dive:
1) Alex: share a redacted session trace (5–10k sessions) or confirm we can use the sample payloads we sent.
2) Procurement: confirm a single point of contact to receive the pilot cost estimate and simple MSA.

Attachments: latency-metrics.csv, pilot-cost-estimate.xlsx (sent privately to procurement)

—
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: latency-metrics.csv (text/csv)]

Looping internally with the pilot scope so we don’t forget the edge items from the call:

Checklist for Tuesday deep-dive / pilot kickoff:
- Confirm model size(s) and sequence length distribution (ask: top 3 workloads).
- Prepare the replay harness + instructions (Karthik).
- Define metrics we’ll collect: p50/p95/p99 per-token, inter-token jitter percentiles, queue depth, GPU utilization, KV hit rate.
- Add automated KV pre-warm script and a short runbook for session affinity options.
- Cost sheet: 48h run cost + estimate for steady-state reserved capacity (Jordan).

Action owners: Karthik = harness + metrics instrumentation; Mina = calendar + customer comms; Jordan = cost + environment provisioning.

I’ll spin up a short internal runbook doc and link to the HubSpot deal later today.
